content.comment_body: Hello, I'm searching for a comprehensive tutorial on setting up Modbus TCP communication between a [product_name] and a power meter. I’m attempting to connect a [product_name] to a third-party WM20 power meter but have not succeeded yet. Both devices can be pinged, meaning they’re on the same network. I appreciate any guidance on this subject.
Which [product_name] model are you using? What are the IP addresses of your [product_name] and the Modbus device? Do you have a link to a manual for the Modbus device along with its register list?
Do you have the correct communication module, specifically the M C ETH?

I’m working with a [product_name] [version_no]. The [product_name] has IP address 192.168.0.3, and the power meter is at 192.168.0.10. The communication module in use is M C ETH. Here is a link to the device manual, including registers: [url]
Did you enable Modbus access in the file properties?
Yes, I have enabled it.
Can you share your program? Please upload it as a ZIP file.
Here is the file.
Why are there two Modbus client connections set up on the same port?
That was not intentional. I thought the left connection was not linked. I assume only the right connection to the power meter should be present. I need help getting this configured properly.
Which port have you set for the Modbus device?
Please try this approach ...
After uploading and running an online test, I’m seeing the AM1 and AM2 values change; they switch between 0.0 and 32767.0 and back to 0.0.
It seems the connection is active now. Go online, use the data table with these settings, and take a screenshot.
The values keep changing continuously.
Sorry, register addresses 30000 and higher refer to input registers (IR), rather than holding registers (HR). Update your Modbus connection table from HR to IR.
The values are still fluctuating.
Go online and use the Online Test feature. Share the online results and screenshots.
I have to leave the office now. I’m very grateful for your help and hope I can get further assistance tomorrow.
To view correct online values, select the F/I blocks. A pair of glasses icon will appear; click on it ...
You’ve selected the wrong data input type. "Double" is a 64-bit type; you need to choose "Float," which is 32-bit.
I overlooked that, but the result is unchanged even with "Float."
I'm sorry, I can't offer further help at this point. I’m unfamiliar with this Modbus device and what configuration it requires.
Thank you for all your help. I'll let you know if I manage to resolve the issue.

I think I’ve identified the problem. The power meter appears to send words in little endian order. I wrote a Python script to switch word order from BIG to LITTLE endian, and now the values read correctly. Bit order is BIG endian, word order is LITTLE endian. Is it possible to swap word order in [product_name]?
There's no standard block for swapping. You’ll need to manually handle this in your program by reading and writing to a different part of the VM memory.
What kind of swap do you mean? Do you want to swap words (W1, W2 > W2, W1) or bytes individually (B1, B2, B3, B4 > B4, B3, B2, B1)?
Yes, you can swap words within your program.
Thank you! It’s working now. The meter display shows 235.4V and 118.1V.
